lines.text: A square of butter paper, licked to a shine. Small prints lead off it through the frost, in no hurry.
A whole pound. He'll be walking it off.
A grey cat sits in the middle of the field, washing one paw with great care. It stops, and looks at Eldwin.
Biscuit. Now then. There's a good—
Biscuit has found the one flat stone in the hollow with any sun on it, and doesn't get up.
Forty autumns walking these walls, and you've picked the warmest stone on the lot in a morning.
Come on. Into the coat with you. There's a woman on the Green who'd like a word about her butter.
He allows it. He makes it clear that he is allowing it.
A grey head comes out of the front of his coat, and looks around as if it had arranged all this.
That's him. That's the thief. A whole pound of butter, Eldwin, on fair day.
Look at him. Not one bit sorry.
Here. Take this cheddar, quick, before he finds out I've got it. And thank you, you old goose.
Biscuit opens one eye, finds nothing in it for him, and closes it again.
